title: Engagement Tracking
subtitle: Open rates, clicks, and engagement by channel and campaign · Period filter: Past 30 days
explanation: Engagement Tracking now has a Period filter matching the one on All Reports. Defaulting to Past 30 days, the agent can switch to 7-, 60-, 90-, or 120-day windows or set a custom range — the metrics and engagement trend both respect the selection. The trend chart now shows realistic seasonality: engagement spikes in January (Q1 newsletter + new-year context), drops through Feb-Mar between campaigns, rebounds in April with the Q2 send, drops again, then ramps back up in July when Q3 launches. This pattern is the actual story underneath the averages above, and it's why per-campaign breakdown is useful — quarterly sends drive the peaks. The By-campaign table now shows each campaign's send date, so the rates tie to the calendar — Sandra can see at a glance that the Q2 Check-in (Apr 8) drove the trend chart's April peak, that the Mid-Quarter Plan Tips just went out on May 20 (which is why its rates show '—'), and that Welcome and Rx Refill are continuous campaigns rather than discrete sends. The table now follows a consistent rule: any campaign that's been sent (or is actively sending, like Welcome and Rx Refill) shows real open and click rates. Anything not yet sent shows 'Pending' with '—' rates. Mid-Quarter Plan Tips is the upcoming Q2 mid-quarter send — Sandra can see at a glance that it's queued but hasn't gone out yet. Rx Refill, being personalized and timely, hits 62.4% open / 28.6% click — far above the quarterly broadcast averages because the content is immediately relevant to each recipient. The KPI compare labels are now 'vs prior year' instead of the static 'vs Q1', which paired badly with the new Period dropdown — when the agent picks 'Past 7 days', comparing to all of Q1 makes no sense. Year-over-year is the durable baseline. The By-channel table also got Facebook a proper click-through metric (2.3%) — previously the row showed '2.3% (CTR)' in the engagement column with '—' in CTR, which was a workaround we no longer need. By-campaign now has an Actions column with a View button on every row — Sandra can jump straight from the engagement report to any campaign's detail page without navigating back to the Campaigns hub. By-channel adds raw-count context (Sent / Views / Clicks) so the agent can see absolute volume alongside the relative rates: Email carries the bulk of the work (45k sent, 14k views, 5.7k clicks), SMS punches well above its weight on engagement rate but is a small-volume channel, and Facebook reaches 13k people but converts low — useful for awareness, weak for action.

title: Monthly IFP — Medicare Transition Report
subtitle: Members transitioning IFP → Medicare in the next 60 days · 1,240 members · 41% high fit
explanation: BookCover identifies every Individual-plan (IFP) member who's aging into Medicare in the next 60 days, scores each one's fit against the carrier's available Medicare plans (network overlap, premium math, plan-type preference), and produces this monthly report. The donut shows the cohort split: 41% high fit (the recommended Medicare plan covers their existing care relationships well + premium math works out), 38% medium, 21% low. The table makes the math visible for each member — current IFP premium and doctor count on the left, recommended Medicare plan + premium + doctor match on the right, with a green/red difference column showing exactly how much the transition saves (or costs) per month. The table now has a filter bar so Sandra can narrow the cohort to just the high-fit members (most likely to convert with a simple outbound call) or just low-fit (who need a more involved consultation). The Download CSV button in the footer pulls the currently-filtered set — useful for handing off to the carrier's licensed agent team for follow-up outreach.

title: Settings
subtitle: Workflow defaults, integrations, notifications, display preferences
explanation: Settings holds the agent's account-wide preferences — defaults that apply to every campaign the system drafts, plus the status of the integrations BookCover depends on (email sender, Facebook Ads Manager, the carrier claims feed). Accessible from the left nav on every screen, separated from the workflow items.

explanation: My Account is the agent's personal profile — what appears on outbound emails and what the system uses to identify them. Separated from Settings because these are identity-level fields, not workflow defaults. Sign-out lives here too.
